newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clinton envoy in Israel in fresh peace bid.
newsitem.headline: Clinton envoy in Israel in fresh peace bid.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton's lead Middle East peacemaker arrived in Israel on Wednesday, launching a new mission to revive talks paralysed by nearly two months of crisis, a U.S. official said.
Dennis Ross was scheduled to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem later on Wednesday.

Ross, in his second shuttle mission within a month, had also been scheduled to travel to self-ruled Gaza for overnight talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, but PLO officials said the meeting had been postponed until Thursday.
Before Ross's arrival Israel played down expectations of "dramatic developments" in its deadlocked peace negotiations with the Palestinians.
The American envoy's visit follows a meeting between Israeli President Ezer Weizman and Arafat on Tuesday at the Israel-Gaza border which failed to break the impasse.
The Weizman-Arafat meeting was only the second high-level Israeli-PLO contact since talks deadlocked in March when Israel began a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Weizman, whose post is largely ceremonial, said after the meeting that Arafat had agreed to resume security coordination between the sides.
But Palestinians said they would insist on a halt to Jewish settlement activities on Israeli-occupied Arab land.
Netanyahu aide David Bar-Illan said settlement construction would go on.
"We obviously are not going to stop building in the settlements any more than the Palestinians are going to stop building in their towns," he told Reuters.
Jewish settlers rebuilt on Wednesday a shack demolished a day earlier by Israeli police near the West Bank settlement of Yitzhar.
Police forcibly removed on Tuesday dozens of settlers from a shack outside the Yitzhar settlement and destroyed the shack along with two other wooden structures they said were built illegally.
Several children, who had been in the shack, were lightly injured by shards of glass and 18 settlers were arrested.

Israel captured the West Bank and Gaza in the 1967 Middle East War. More than 130,000 Israeli have since settled amid some two million Palestinians in the occupied areas, not counting Arab East Jerusalem.
Ross's last trip in April was overshadowed by a domestic Israeli crisis and failed to achieve any breakthrough.
